req.title: Health probe returns liveness
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET /health/ with HTTP 200 and a status:'ok' JSON body.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that GET /health/ returns HTTP 200 with a JSON body containing status:'ok'. To achieve high mutation kill rate: (1) positive EP test asserts exact status code 200 AND exact JSON body {'status':'ok'} — catches constant mutations on status code and string mutations on the key/value; (2) negative NEG test issues a POST to /health/ to confirm the endpoint is GET-only (expects 405) — catches mutations that accidentally broaden method acceptance; (3) boundary BVA test asserts the Content-Type header is application/json — catches mutations that change response serialization; (4) DT test asserts the response body has exactly one key 'status' with value exactly 'ok' (not 'OK', not 'okay') — catches string-constant mutations; (5) STC test verifies idempotency by calling GET /health/ twice and asserting both responses are identical — catches state-mutation bugs.

tests.name: test_health_get_returns_200_and_status_ok
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
health_route is registered on the app
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

def test_health_get_returns_200_and_status_ok():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert body == {"status": "ok"}
    assert body["status"] == "ok"
    assert len(body) == 1

Value of 'status' is exactly the string 'ok' (lowercase, not 'OK' or 'okay')
No extra keys present in the body
trace: R-PLAYER-016: status:'ok' — exact string constant, exact key name
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

def test_health_body_key_is_exactly_status_value_is_exactly_ok():
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/health/")
    assert response.status_code == 200
    body = response.json()
    assert "status" in body
    assert body["status"] == "ok"
    assert body["status"] != "OK"
    assert body["status"] != "okay"
    assert body["status"] != ""
    assert list(body.keys()) == ["status"]

tests.name: test_health_idempotent_on_repeated_calls
preconditions: FastAPI app is importable from main
actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
expected: Both calls return identical JSON body {"status": "ok"}
trace: R-PLAYER-016: liveness probe must be idempotent (STC — no state transition)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

def test_health_idempotent_on_repeated_calls():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.get("/health/")
    r2 = client.get("/health/")
    assert r1.status_code == 200
    assert r2.status_code == 200
    assert r1.json() == {"status": "ok"}
    assert r2.json() == {"status": "ok"}
    assert r1.json() == r2.json()

actions: Instantiate TestClient with the FastAPI app
expected: Response indicates the path is not found or redirected
trace: R-PLAYER-016 error pathway: wrong path -> not HTTP 200
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from main import app

def test_health_wrong_path_returns_404():
    client = TestClient(app, follow_redirects=False)
    response = client.get("/health")
    assert response.status_code != 200
    assert response.status_code in (301, 307, 308, 404)
